overlay_generator.byte_identity: strip the four generated ACSL annotations to obtain unchanged production source

preconditions: valid read-only array of count receipt-v1 records
null trusted head or 32-byte readable trusted head
conclusions: On TB_OK the genesis has no predecessor
On TB_OK each later receipt has a predecessor flag and matching predecessor hash bytes
On TB_OK the supplied trusted head, if any, equals the final recorded hash bytes
No writes to caller-owned receipt or trusted-head memory
assumptions: equal32 is pure and returns true iff its two readable 32-byte inputs have identical bytes; its memcmp implementation NOT separately proved in this milestone
calculate_hash reads one receipt, writes only its separate 32-byte output and returns one of listed statuses; no correctness of the 32-byte SHA result is assumed or proved
C caller memory valid, object and size_t semantics as defined by explicit target platform model
exclusions: No proof of SHA-256, OpenSSL, HACL* or true digest value
No proof of full canonical receipt parser or JSON encoder or hash-domain refinement
No assertion of independent anchor custody, authorship, timestamps, real deletion or physical erasure
No proof of GCC, Clang, Rust, system libraries, kernel, firmware or hardware
Null/invalid-count argument paths are separately covered by Phase 17 and not within Phase 18 valid-input contract
